Replace.Text: Settlers cost 10% less [ICON_Gold] Gold to purchase. Domestic [ICON_TradeRoute] Trade Routes sent from a city with a Suguba provide +2 [ICON_Production] Production. +1 [ICON_TradeRoute] Trade Route capacity for each continent on which you own at least three cities that you founded (maximum +4).

Every tile of a city that holds at least one Wonder has +1 Appeal. In a city with a Grove, +5% [ICON_Production] Production toward Wonders for each Breathtaking tile adjacent to the Wonder being built, up to +20% (counted at the start of your turn). Great Wall segments adjacent to another segment provide +1 [ICON_Faith] Faith.

Cities you found on Hills gain +1 [ICON_Production] Production and +10% [ICON_Production] Production toward Settlers. They also gain +25% [ICON_Production] Production toward districts until their first specialty district is complete.

Unimproved Rainforest tiles adjacent to a Preserve provide +1 [ICON_Culture] Culture once Medieval Faires is known. Cities with at least three Rainforest tiles gain +10% [ICON_Production] Production toward Wonders. In a city that holds at least one Wonder, each Rainforest provides a further +1 Appeal to adjacent tiles.

The caravans of Mali carry more than salt and gold: they carry the next city. Buy your Settlers, plant them on every shore you can reach, and let the trade that binds them together pay for the ones that follow.
A Wonder is only as fine as the land that frames it. Tend the groves, choose each site as a painter chooses where the mountain stands, and the empire itself becomes the garden.

From the high plateau every valley looks like an invitation. Found your cities where the ground rises, and each one will be quick to raise its first quarter and quicker still to send out the next band of settlers.
Leave the forest standing and it will repay you. Under its canopy rise Wonders the world will cross oceans to see, and every one of them makes the green around it lovelier still.
